prompt: What does audit.js do with the five tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa?

choices.text: It reports which WCAG version the page was written for
choices.why: A page does not declare a version; the tags choose what to test it against.

choices.text: It runs only the rules filed under WCAG A and AA
choices.why: Right. That is "WCAG 2.2 AA" as a list of rules, without the best-practice ones.

choices.text: It sorts the violations so the AA ones print last
choices.why: They filter; they do not sort.

choices.text: It adds the best-practice rules on top of the WCAG ones
choices.why: The opposite: best-practice rules carry their own tag and are left out.

prompt: Why does audit.js wait for networkidle before calling analyze()?
hint: Where does the list of shows come from?

choices.text: axe needs the network to download its rules
choices.why: The rules ship inside the package; nothing is downloaded at audit time.

choices.text: Playwright refuses to evaluate scripts on a page still loading
choices.why: It does not refuse; it would simply audit whatever existed at that instant.

choices.text: A fetch fills the page after load, and the audit must see it
choices.why: Right. An audit of a half-drawn page is an audit of a different page.

choices.text: Lighthouse is still running in the background
choices.why: Lighthouse has nothing to do with audit.js.

prompt: Which defects of book.html did audit.js report? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the missing lang
choices.why: Right: html-has-lang.

choices.text: the grey note
choices.why: Right: color-contrast, at 2.84.

choices.text: the removed focus outline
choices.why: No rule can tell a missing indicator from a different one.

choices.text: the logo without alt
choices.why: Right: image-alt.

choices.text: the div used as a button
choices.why: Nothing in the document says the div was meant to be pressed.

choices.text: the name field without a label
choices.why: Right: label.

prompt: What axe could not decide comes back in the list called ___, and audit.js prints it as work for a person.
Which alt text is right for the logo, an image of the word boxoffice?
hint: A logo's alternative is what it says.

choices.text: logo
choices.why: That names the kind of thing, not what it says.

choices.text: boxoffice
choices.why: Right. The text in the picture is the text alternative.

choices.text: A dark red rectangle with white letters
choices.why: A description of the colours tells nobody anything they need.

choices.text: logo.svg, 200 by 48
choices.why: A file name and a size are what a reader says when alt is missing.

prompt: audit.js reports 0 violations on book2.html. What is a true sentence for the test report?
hint: Say which tool, which rules, which state.

choices.text: book2.html conforms to WCAG 2.2 at level AA
choices.why: Four defects remain, and none of them is a rule axe has.

choices.text: axe's WCAG A and AA rules pass on book2.html as it loads
choices.why: Right. That is what the run measured, and no more.

choices.text: book2.html is accessible to keyboard and screen reader users
choices.why: The Book control still cannot be reached from the keyboard.

choices.text: book2.html has no defects that a person would find
choices.why: A person finds three straight away, with the Tab key.

prompt: A third-party chat widget fails color-contrast and the team cannot change it. What should the gate do?
hint: An exclusion is a sentence, or it is a hole.

choices.text: Drop color-contrast from the tags so the build goes green
choices.why: That stops contrast being checked on every page you do own.

choices.text: Keep failing every build until the vendor ships a fix
choices.why: A gate that is always red gets ignored, and then it guards nothing.

choices.text: Exclude that one element, with a comment saying why
choices.why: Right. The rule keeps running everywhere else, and the hole is written down.

choices.text: Stop running axe and audit that page by hand from now on
choices.why: The rest of the page still deserves the automated check.

prompt: What accessibility score did Lighthouse give book2.html, out of 100?
Lighthouse reported tabindex on book.html and audit.js did not. Why?

choices.text: The rule is tagged best-practice, which audit.js leaves out
choices.why: Right. Lighthouse runs best-practice rules too.

choices.text: Lighthouse uses its own engine, which knows more than axe
choices.why: Its accessibility audits are axe rules underneath.

choices.text: audit.js ran before the page's script set the tabindex
choices.why: The tabindex is in the markup from the start.

choices.text: Positive tabindex fails 2.4.3, which only Lighthouse checks
choices.why: No rule decides 2.4.3; the tabindex rule is a best practice.

prompt: Match each WAVE category to what it holds.
hint: Some are faults and some are not.

pairs.right: what is right, such as every alt
headings and landmarks, the page's outline

prompt: Why can wave.webaim.org not audit book.html in the course's VM, when the extension can?

choices.text: The site refuses pages that are served over plain HTTP
choices.why: Not the reason here; the address is the problem.

choices.text: WebAIM's servers fetch the page, and they cannot reach the VM
choices.why: Right. The extension runs in your browser, which can.

choices.text: The site needs an account, the extension does not
choices.why: Neither needs one for this.

choices.text: The site checks only contrast
choices.why: It runs the same checks as the extension.

prompt: Why did no rule report the div used as the Book button?
hint: What would the rule have to know?

choices.text: The div is hidden from the accessibility tree
choices.why: It is in the tree, as text.

choices.text: axe skips elements that have event handlers
choices.why: It does not skip them; nothing in a handler tells it what the element is for.

choices.text: Nothing in the document says it was meant to be pressed
choices.why: Right. Purpose is not decidable from markup.

choices.text: Its text, Book, passes the contrast check
choices.why: Contrast is unrelated to whether it can be operated.

prompt: A page has alt="image" on a photograph of the theatre's stage. What does axe's image-alt rule say?
hint: The rule checks that a name exists.

choices.text: It fails, because "image" is on a list of banned words
choices.why: The rule asks for a name, and "image" is one.

choices.text: It passes, and a person has to judge the text
choices.why: Right. A rule checks that the name exists, not that it says what the picture says.

choices.text: It lands in incomplete, because axe cannot see photographs
choices.why: It has nothing to look at; the attribute is present and the rule is satisfied.

choices.text: It fails 1.1.1, since the text is shorter than five letters
choices.why: No length is required, and short alternatives can be right.

prompt: Order the tools by how many of book.html's eight defects they reported, fewest first.
hint: Three, four and five are not all the numbers.
items: axe, Lighthouse and a person with a keyboard and a screen reader

prompt: A release note says "Accessibility: Lighthouse 100". What is the best question to ask before signing it off?
hint: The score weighs only what was audited.

choices.text: Was it run in both light and dark mode?
choices.why: Worth knowing, but even both at 100 leave the manual items untested.

choices.text: Who checked the manual items and the keyboard?
choices.why: Right. The score cannot see what no audit measured, such as a div that cannot be reached.

choices.text: Was the score above 90 on the previous release too?
choices.why: A trend in the score says nothing about the undecidable defects.

choices.text: Was Lighthouse run with --no-sandbox?
choices.why: That flag changes how Chromium starts, not what it audits.

prompt: The error state of book2.html appears only after Book is pressed with an empty name. How should the suite audit it?
hint: axe sees the document as it is when analyze() runs.

choices.text: Run audit.js twice, since the second run sees more
choices.why: Both runs see the page as it loads.

choices.text: Nothing is needed: axe evaluates every state a script can reach
choices.why: It evaluates one document, the one that exists at that moment.

choices.text: Add the best-practice tag, which covers dynamic content
choices.why: No tag reaches a state the page has not entered.

choices.text: Press Book with the name empty first, then call analyze()
choices.why: Right. Each state is a different document, audited when it exists.

prompt: A manager proposes dropping the manual keyboard pass, because axe now runs on every commit. What is the strongest reply?
hint: Look at the three defects nothing reported.

choices.text: axe reports false positives, so its results need a person
choices.why: Its violations are nearly always right; the gap is what it never reports.

choices.text: The defects that stop a booking were the ones axe cannot see
choices.why: Right. The div and the invisible focus passed every rule.

choices.text: Running axe on every commit is too slow for the pipeline
choices.why: Speed is not the argument; the audit took seconds.

choices.text: WCAG requires a human signature on every conformance claim
choices.why: WCAG asks for no signature; the point is what tools can decide.
